chunks: From him, from Salama, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shammam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, condolences came to them; a messenger arrived whom they heard but did not see in person, so he said: 'Peace be upon you, O People of the Household, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.'

Every soul shall taste death, but you shall only be paid your full reward on the Day of Resurrection; then whoever is removed far from the Fire and is admitted to Paradise, he indeed has succeeded. And what is the life of the world except the enjoyment of delusion.

In Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is consolation for every calamity and a replacement for every deceased one, and a attainment for what is lost. So rely on Allah and hope in Him, for the deprived one is he who is deprived of the reward. And peace be upon you.
ai.seo_question: What did the messenger say to the Ahl al-Bayt upon the death of the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records the divine consolation offered to the Ahl al-Bayt upon the Prophet's death, where a messenger (often identified as Jibril) recited verses affirming the inevitability of death and the fleeting nature of worldly life. It highlights the Shia theological perspective that Allah serves as the ultimate comforter and successor to all the deceased, urging believers to place their trust in Him for eternal reward. The narration underscores the transition from earthly grief to spiritual hope, framing the Prophet's death not as an end but as a passage to divine proximity.
